title: MLPC 07 - Feed-Forward Neural Networks
subject: Machine Learning and Pattern Classification
description: Covers neurons, activation functions, gradient descent, backpropagation, learning modes, overfitting, and neural-network classification. All questions are single-choice and modeled after the conceptual style of the MLPC Retry 2024S exam. Source: 07_Neural_Networks.pdf.

questions.question: What does a standard artificial neuron compute before applying its activation function?

options.text: The unweighted median of all labels
A weighted sum of inputs plus a bias

questions.explanation: A neuron first forms an affine combination of its inputs, then applies an activation.

questions.question: Why are nonlinear hidden activations important in an MLP?

options.text: Without them, stacked affine layers still represent only an affine function

questions.explanation: Composing linear or affine layers without nonlinearities does not create a nonlinear model.

questions.question: A network with enough hidden units and a suitable nonlinear activation is called a universal function approximator because it can:

options.text: Approximate a broad class of functions arbitrarily well
Find the global optimum in one step

questions.explanation: The approximation result concerns representational capacity, not optimization or generalisation guarantees.

questions.question: Gradient descent updates a parameter theta using which direction?
questions.explanation: The negative gradient points in the direction of steepest local decrease of the loss.

questions.question: What is the main role of the learning rate eta?

options.text: Scale the size of each parameter update

questions.explanation: The learning rate controls how far the parameters move along the update direction.

questions.question: What can happen if the learning rate is much too large?

options.text: The loss may oscillate or diverge

questions.explanation: Oversized updates can repeatedly overshoot useful regions and destabilize training.

questions.question: Why is backpropagation needed in a multilayer network?

options.text: Hidden units have no direct target values, so their contribution to output error must be propagated backward
The training set has no inputs

questions.explanation: Backpropagation applies the chain rule to assign gradients to hidden-layer parameters.

questions.question: Which order describes one backpropagation training iteration?

options.text: Update labels, remove inputs, create folds
Forward pass, compute output error, propagate error backward, update weights

questions.explanation: Activations are computed forward and gradients are then computed backward.

questions.question: How does online learning differ from full-batch learning?

options.text: Online learning updates after individual examples; batch learning accumulates gradients over the dataset
They differ only in output activation

questions.explanation: The difference is when and from how much data each weight update is computed.

questions.question: Why can adding too many hidden units increase overfitting risk?

options.text: It reduces the number of parameters
It increases model capacity and the ability to fit noise
It forces every output to zero

questions.explanation: More units generally mean more parameters and a more expressive, higher-variance model.

questions.question: In early stopping, when should training usually stop?

options.text: When validation error begins to worsen while training continues to improve
Only after training error is exactly zero

questions.explanation: A rising validation error indicates that continued fitting is harming generalisation.

questions.question: A binary classifier uses one identity output trained with squared error and targets -1 and +1. Is its raw output automatically a probability?

options.text: Yes, because every neural output is a probability
No, an identity output is not constrained to [0,1]
No, because binary tasks cannot use neural networks

questions.explanation: This setup learns a discriminant score; probability interpretation requires an appropriate output transformation and loss.

questions.question: Which output/loss pairing is appropriate for probabilistic binary classification?

options.text: Identity and entropy of the input

questions.explanation: Sigmoid constrains one output to [0,1], and binary cross-entropy matches Bernoulli targets.

questions.question: Which output/loss pairing is standard for mutually exclusive k-class classification?

options.text: k softmax outputs and categorical cross-entropy
k linear outputs with no decision rule
One sigmoid for every input feature

questions.explanation: Softmax produces a normalized class distribution, and categorical cross-entropy scores the one-hot target.
